newsitem.title: USA: Nynex sets pact in step to offer long-distance service.
newsitem.headline: Nynex sets pact in step to offer long-distance service.

text.p: Nynex Corp. said Tuesday it reached an agreement with AT&T Corp. to boost competition in its local phone market, moving the regional phone company a step closer to entering the lucrative long-distance market in New York.
The deal would allow long distance provider AT&T to begin offering local phone service in New York state.
The regional telephone company said it agreed to connect its network with that of AT&T, the nation's largest long-distance company, and submitted the agreement for approval by regulators.

If approved by the state Public Service Commission, the pact will open Nynex's local phone network to AT&T, further paving the way for Nynex to seek approval to enter the long-distance market in its home territory, the company said.

Under the telecommunications laws passed last year, regional Bell companies had to open their local phone markets to competition. If regulators agree that a local company has met requirements under the law, it can enter the long-distance market in its home territory.

Suzanne Berman, a spokeswoman for AT&T, said it was the first deal AT&T had reached in the Nynex's six-state service region. AT&T has signed and won approval from state regulators for 15 such deals with Baby Bell local service companies in other states.

While the entry of the leading U.S. long distance companies into the densely populated New York metro region market promises to hasten process of local competition, analysts said that wide scale competition throughout the United States is unlikely to occur before the year 2000.
Nynex also said that MCI Communications Corp., the No. 2 long-distance carrier, recently withdrew a complaint against Nynex and signed an agreement to connect the companies' networks in New York.
That pact has been given to arbitrators who are expected to complete the details and submit the deal to regulators for approval shortly after the AT&T agreement.

Nynex and Bell Atlantic are awaiting final approval from U.S. regulators on their proposed merger, announced last year, which would form the nation's largest local phone company in terms of revenues, and would stretch from Maine to Virginia.
